import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
HID = 32
LAYOUTS = [(0, ()), (1, ()), (0, (2,)), (0, (3,))]


def to_layouts(m, T, Y, X):
    B = m.shape[0]
    bases = [m.reshape(B, T, Y, X), m.reshape(B, T, X, Y).permute(0, 1, 3, 2)]
    out = []
    for k, f in LAYOUTS:
        g = bases[k]
        if len(f) > 0:
            g = g.flip(f)
        out.append(g)
    return torch.cat(out, dim=1)


def from_layouts(o, T, Y, X):
    B = o.shape[0]
    o = o.reshape(B, len(LAYOUTS), T, Y, X)
    total = 0
    for i, (k, f) in enumerate(LAYOUTS):
        g = o[:, i]
        if len(f) > 0:
            g = g.flip(f)
        if k == 1:
            g = g.permute(0, 1, 3, 2)
        total = total + g.reshape(B, -1)
    return total


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.T, self.Y, self.X = spec.n_types, spec.Y, spec.X
        self.n_place = spec.n_place
        L = len(LAYOUTS)
        cin = spec.in_channels + L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.hid = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(HID, L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.out.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        T, Y, X = self.T, self.Y, self.X
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].float()
        mc = to_layouts(m, T, Y, X)
        yy = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xx = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        s = self.stem(torch.cat([obs, mc, yy, xx], dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        o = self.out(F.relu(self.hid(f)))
        place = from_layouts(o, T, Y, X)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

    bases = [m.reshape(B, T, Y, X), m.reshape(B, T, X, Y).permute(0, 1, 3, 2)]

        g = bases[k]
        if len(f) > 0:
            g = g.flip(f)
        out.append(g)
    return torch.cat(out, dim=1)


def from_layouts(o, T, Y, X):
    B = o.shape[0]
    o = o.reshape(B, len(LAYOUTS), T, Y, X)
    total = 0
    for i, (k, f) in enumerate(LAYOUTS):

        if len(f) > 0:
            g = g.flip(f)
        if k == 1:
            g = g.permute(0, 1, 3, 2)
        total = total + g.reshape(B, -1)
    return total


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.T, self.Y, self.X = spec.n_types, spec.Y, spec.X
        self.n_place = spec.n_place
        L = len(LAYOUTS)
        cin = spec.in_channels + L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.hid = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(HID, L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.out.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        T, Y, X = self.T, self.Y, self.X
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].float()
        mc = to_layouts(m, T, Y, X)
        yy = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xx = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        s = self.stem(torch.cat([obs, mc, yy, xx], dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        x = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        c = F.relu(self.ctx(torch.cat([x.mean((2, 3)), x.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)))

analyses.1: No trials have run in this search yet. Across 84 earlier trials, only one network family scored above 0: the legal-action mask goes in as input channels under four layouts (as given, transposed, y-flipped, x-flipped), and four per-type output maps are re-laid in those same layouts and summed. It reached 0.22 on two recipes. Every other net and recipe scored exactly 0. That points to a world whose action indexing or geometry differs from its description in ways that change between worlds. The mask is the only input in the action's own frame, so a net that sees it and can re-lay its output can learn the mismatch. Round 1 does three things. It reproduces that family here at roughly the starting net's cost, so it gets the full sample budget. It tests a full 8-way dihedral hedge, which would cover a mismatch the 4-layout version misses. It tests a recipe with more samples. The first signal to watch is nonzero late training success.
analyses.2:
Every trial in this world scored about zero, and late training success was 0 in all three. The 4-layout net scored 0 on both recipes. The 8-layout dihedral net had one success in 512 on one seed, which is noise. When a layout matched the world in earlier worlds, this family reached about 0.22. So the mismatch here is probably not a flip or transpose of a [type, Y, X] action layout, and recipe changes will not help until the right layout is found. Two plausible mismatches are not yet covered:
- the action index may be type-minor, a = (y*X + x)*T + t, so a [T,Y,X] reshape scrambles both the mask and the logits;
- DONE may sit at index 0, which shifts every placement index by 1.
This round tests each hedge alone on the 8-layout dihedral net, plus one file that combines both. The 8-layout net is the base because it covers the 4-layout set. All three files cost about the same as the starting net, so each keeps the full sample budget.
analyses.3: Every trial so far is at noise level. The only nonzero seeds came from nets that contain the full 8-layout dihedral [T,Y,X] set: r1c2 scored 0.0039 on one seed, and r2c2 scored 0.002 with training success 0.0002. Adding type-minor layouts (r2c1) or the DONE-first shift on top of the full set (r2c3) did not help, so those two deviations are probably not this world's problem. One untested explanation is the learning procedure. The default recipe gives only 32 PPO updates in the budget (131k steps / 4096 per update), which may be too few policy improvements for an 8x8x6 world with designs of up to 16 bricks. The dihedral net also uses only 0.83 of the compute, and compute below 1x is counted as 1x anyway, so a third residual conv costs no samples. Plan for this round: (A) the dihedral net with 4x more updates, (B) the dihedral net with a deeper trunk at r≈1, (C) a new idea: global-context broadcast plus a deeper trunk, run with the many-updates recipe.
analyses.4: Eight of nine trials scored 0 on both seeds. The best, r1c2 (8 dihedral layouts), reached only 0.002 (one seed at 0.0039), which is within noise. Late training success was 0 or 0.0002 everywhere, so no candidate has learned to build. Hedging the action index more widely did not help: 16 layouts with type-minor order, a DONE-first shift, and both together all scored 0 or 0.001. That argues against an index mismatch. Of the two trunk changes, the 3rd conv and global context, neither helped, and the 128-update recipe also scored 0. The likeliest remaining bottlenecks are credit assignment for the exact-build bonus at the end of each episode, too few useful updates, and trunk capacity. In the last round I keep the dihedral-8 net, which is still the only nonzero result, and change one thing per candidate: a longer-horizon recipe, more steps with a faster learning rate, and a wider trunk paid for with fewer epochs.
